# From Dairy Farm to Dream Home: Discover The Holding Village Neighborhood


Tri Pointe Homes


•


October 14, 2026


Share this article


Located in[Wake Forest](https://www.wakeforestnc.gov/visitors) , North Carolina,[Holding Village](https://www.holdingvillage.com/) sits on[257 acres of land](https://www.readercommunities.com/current-development/holding-village/) once home to the historic Holding family dairy farm. While the community has evolved beyond its agricultural roots, its history remains woven into everyday life. From the preserved silos that still stand over the neighborhood, to the feeling of togetherness that defines the community,[The Mews at Holding Village by Tri Pointe Homes®](https://www.tripointehomes.com/nc/raleigh/mews-at-holding-village) honors its past while creating a place where new memories can take root!


**Living Where the Past Meets the Present**


Long before Holding Village became a place to call home, this land was part of a working dairy farm that played a huge role in the history of Wake Forest. The old dairy farm was comprised of over 800 acres of land, where cows grazed and milk flowed like a river.[According to the Town of Wake Forest,](https://www.wakeforestnc.gov/planning/long-range-planning/historic-preservation/history-wake-forest) the farm, which was once the largest dairy supplier to the[Pine State](https://raleighhistoric.org/items/show/76) Creamery, was built by W.W. Holding. The Holding family was one of Wake Forest’s wealthiest families and they were involved in several businesses around town including a drugstore and the[Royall Cotton Mill](https://wakeforestmuseum.org/royall-cotton-mill/) . The town of Wake Forest historic research notes that Wake County shifted toward dairy farming in the early 20th century.


While the farm is no longer filled with cows and dairy farmers, reminders of its agricultural past remain throughout Holding Village. The original silos now center Silo Park, while Holding Lake continues to be a place where residents can slow down, spend time outdoors and make memories together.


**Keeping the Spirit of the Farm Alive**


In its peaceful acreage, Holding Village echoes a time when life moved a little slower. A life where cows grazed in a nearby pasture and the sound of a distant moo might be the loudest part of the day. The Mews at Holding Village is inspired by that sense of peace and carries it into modern living with amenities that are designed to bring residents together to enjoy the outdoors and the simple moments.


At the center of it all, Holding Lake anchors the community. With its 15 acres of peaceful, spring-fed water, residents can enjoy kayaking, paddle boarding and taking in its idyllic views. This tranquil scene allows residents to slow down, let free of their anxieties, perhaps even bring their heart rates down from the busy day-to-day. For residents hoping to get their heart rates up, the community offers miles of trails for running, walking or strolling through the sites. Take laps around the lake, by the silos or simply through the beautifully designed neighborhood. The trails also connect hikers to the[Wake Forest Greenway System](https://www.wakeforestnc.gov/parks-recreation-cultural-resources/greenways) at the[Dunn Creek Greenway](https://www.wakeforestnc.gov/parks-recreation-cultural-resources/greenways/trails/dunn-creek-greenway) and[Smith Creek Soccer Center](https://www.wakeforestnc.gov/parks-recreation-cultural-resources/parks-facilities/smith-creek-soccer-center) .


Silo Park, a unique addition to the community, places the past right into the present. The old Holding Dairy Farm silos stand tall at the center of the park, reminding parkgoers of what once was there. The tall, impossible to miss silos give an almost cinematic feeling to the area, making it ideal for people looking for a whimsical touch to their everyday. The park isn’t just there to make residents feel like they stepped out of a postcard, it serves the community by being a fun place to relax with lawn games and picnics or simply enjoy an open green space!


Somerset Pavilion serves a similar purpose. The pavilion features a beautiful community pool, dock access for the lake, playground and picnic tables, making a relaxing warm day easy to accomplish. As the day winds down, the pavilion is the perfect spot to catch the sun setting over Holding Lake. From poolside afternoons to peaceful evenings by the water, Somerset Pavilion makes it easy to slow down and enjoy a few of the many amenities the community has to offer.


**Where History Becomes Home**


For homebuyers looking for a home that meets their needs while offering something more through its community, Holding Village delivers. The Mews at Holding Village offers 2- and 3-story townhomes ranging from 1,720 to 2,317 square feet, with 3-4 bedrooms, 2.5-3.5 bathrooms and 2-bay garages.


But here, home is about more than what’s behind your front door. It’s about being part of a community that celebrates its history while creating new memories every day! Though the dairy farm is no longer home to grazing cows, its story is still alive throughout Holding Village in the preserved silos, the lake, the open spaces and the sense of togetherness woven into the community. At Holding Village, the past isn’t simply remembered, it’s part of what makes this place feel like home.


Ready to make Holding Village a part of your story? Discover the charm of this community and find your place at[The Mews at Holding Village](https://www.tripointehomes.com/nc/raleigh/mews-at-holding-village) by Tri Pointe Homes. Explore available homes and learn more about life in this one-of-a-kind Wake Forest community today!
